title: Alerts filed by type
prompt: The alerts desk usually opens one kind of alert at a time. Write `save(weather_alerts, path)` so it saves the alerts as Parquet with one folder per `alert_type`. `solve` is written for you: it saves them and reads the folder back.
rules: The folder may already hold an earlier save: replace it, don't add to it.
`solve` returns what reading the folder gives: the other columns in their order, then `alert_type` last.
Keep every alert, repeated rows included. An alert with no type is kept too.
hints: `write.partitionBy("column")` puts each value's rows in its own `column=value` folder.
Reading the top folder adds the partition column back as the last column.
Writing to a folder that exists needs `.mode("overwrite")`; `append` would keep the old rows too.
explanation: `weather_alerts.write.mode("overwrite").partitionBy("alert_type").parquet(path)` writes one folder per type. The type lives in the folder name, so reading the top folder puts `alert_type` back as the last column, which is how the expected result is shaped. An alert with no type goes into a special default folder and reads back as missing. Partitioning by a different column moves that column to the end instead, and without `overwrite` the second save fails because the folder exists.
